title: I only ask Gemini one question, but I can't solve problems without it
excerpt: Gemini and Google Search work best together
content_html:
Published Sep 4, 2026, 7:00 AM EDT

Jon Gilbert is a Features Writer for Android Police. I've covered Android since 2021, focusing on writing features and guides about Android apps and features that directly affect users. I've attended CES to uncover powerful hardware that isn't dominated by Google like the Mudita Kompakt. I trawl through Android news daily, hunting for stories that have real-world consequences. I hold a BA in History & Classics. 

Since Gemini launched in December 2023, I've struggled to make use of the tool.

Google has worked tirelessly to integrate it with the various Google apps I use, but none of the new tools unlocked by Gemini have replaced my existing tools (that is, my brain).

A few tools have been situationally useful. Pixel Screenshots helped me find a Christmas gift, and I use Circle to Search from time to time.

However, I've noticed myself reaching for Gemini when presented with a unique situation, and I've realized that it's become a small but crucial asset.

What do I do when I don't know what the problem is?

Google Search is my first port of call 99% of the time

Let's say I boot up my computer, and I'm presented with an error code. Or that I spot a new store and want to know about its opening hours. Or maybe my desk chair is broken, and I need a new one.

To solve each of these problems, I could turn to Gemini or Google Search. Both can answer my question, but I always turn to the latter.

While Gemini usually gives me a reasonable answer, I always have to verify its responses. By skipping straight to the sources, I save time.

But have you spotted the common pattern in my queries? It's that I knew what the problem was and how to search for it.

Google has served me faithfully in this regard since the first days of Google Search, and it still works.

I turn to Gemini when I don't know what the problem is

It's what I search with when I don't know what to search

Around two months ago, I booted up my computer and was presented with this lovely error on my monitor:

I needed to solve the problem urgently, as I didn't have a laptop or spare monitor on hand. But what was I to search for?

I tried "flickering blue and pink patches on computer monitor on startup," but I was greeted with a labyrinth of potential problems and fixes. I needed it solved quickly, so I turned to Gemini.

I took a picture of my screen and asked Gemini what was wrong. Gemini listed potential causes, then provided troubleshooting steps for each problem.

With Gemini's help, I ticked off the potential causes until I arrived at two potential problems, both related to the monitor's hardware.

I verified these causes with a traditional Google Search and found that they could cause the display errors I was witnessing.

Unfortunately, the monitor was broken and out of warranty, but I was able to order a replacement for the next day and not miss too much work.

I only use Gemini to answer one simple question

No matter the wording, it's always the same

I realized that I had been using Gemini infrequently to answer the same question every time. Whether it was a monitor malfunction, a strange bug, or a tool I didn't recognize, my question was "What is this?"

Gemini is fantastic for answering this question. When I know what something is, I know what to ask next. I can search for fixes for the malfunction, find out if the bug bites (it was a wolf spider, so I backed away fairly rapidly), or find out how the tool works (it was a particularly strange box-cutter).

Every time I ask Gemini "What is this?" I accompany my query with an image. This helps me quickly verify its answers and ensures that I receive the most accurate responses.

What hasn't changed is that I still check sources to verify Gemini's answers. I still don't trust Gemini, but it always manages to put me on the right track.

I use Gemini and Google Search in tandem

They work beautifully together

I know a few people who use Gemini for everything, and I understand why. But the technology isn't there yet to make it my go-to option for answering every question I have.

For example, I never ask Gemini to fact-check. Not just because it can hallucinate incorrect answers, but because a poorly worded question can result in a technically correct answer.

Gemini helps me identify what I need to ask, and Google Search helps me answer the resultant question. It's a perfect relationship that has made me wonder if I'll ever need another tool.

Use tools for what they're best at, not what they're advertised for

I don't use Gemini for 99% of the ways Google suggests I use it for. I haven't found it superior to thinking about my problem.

Sure, there are situational uses for it (and I really wish I had NotebookLM back in college), but it doesn't work for me the way Google wants it to.

Instead, Gemini answers the simple question "What is this?" and then I ignore it for another month. Thanks, Gemini.
